cards.q: What is PVST+ and what is its core architecture?
cards.a: PVST+ (Per-VLAN Spanning Tree Plus) is Cisco's per-VLAN STP implementation that runs a separate 802.1D-style STP instance for each VLAN, each independently electing a Root Bridge, Root Ports, Designated Ports, and Blocking Ports.

cards.q: How does PVST+ enable per-VLAN Layer-2 load balancing?
cards.a: Because every VLAN has its own spanning-tree instance, the same physical interface can forward one VLAN while blocking another, so different VLANs can use different forwarding paths across redundant links.

cards.q: What STP mode do modern Cisco switches commonly default to?
cards.a: Modern Cisco switches commonly default to Rapid PVST+, not classic PVST+.

cards.q: How are PVST+ BPDUs carried on an 802.1Q trunk regarding tagging?
cards.a: Native-VLAN BPDUs are untagged, and PVST+ BPDUs for other (non-native) VLANs are 802.1Q tagged. There is additional special VLAN 1/CST interoperability handling.

cards.q: Why is it an oversimplification to say only the native VLAN BPDU is untagged on a PVST+ trunk?
cards.a: PVST+ interoperates with IEEE CST through VLAN 1 by default: Cisco sends the IEEE-formatted VLAN 1/CST BPDU untagged for interoperability, while PVST+ BPDUs for other VLANs are tagged; if the native VLAN differs from VLAN 1, the native-VLAN BPDU is also untagged.

cards.q: What can a native VLAN mismatch cause on a PVST+ trunk?
cards.a: PVST+ inconsistency, because the switches associate untagged BPDUs with different VLANs. Cisco uses PVST+ consistency checking to detect this condition.

cards.q: How does the Extended System ID make each VLAN's Bridge ID unique in PVST+?
cards.a: The 12-bit VLAN ID is incorporated into the priority field so each VLAN has a unique Bridge ID. Effective priority = configured priority + VLAN ID (e.g., 4096 + VLAN 10 = 4106), and configured priority uses increments of 4096.

cards.q: What is the default configurable PVST+ bridge priority?
How does PVST+ elect a Root Bridge for a VLAN, and can different VLANs have different roots?
cards.a: PVST+ elects a Root Bridge independently for every VLAN using the lowest Bridge ID (lowest effective priority, then lowest MAC). This allows different VLANs to have different Root Bridges and forwarding paths.

cards.q: Which port role does the Root Bridge have, and what are the roles on a non-root switch?
cards.a: The Root Bridge has no Root Port; its active ports are normally Designated Ports. A non-root switch selects one Root Port per VLAN and each segment has one Designated Port; redundant paths become non-forwarding/blocking.

cards.q: In classic PVST+, what is the role of a redundant, non-forwarding path called, and is Alternate one of its roles?
cards.a: In classic PVST+/802.1D it is called a Blocking port. Alternate is an RSTP/Rapid PVST+ role; classic PVST+ does not use Alternate as a formal role.

cards.q: What are the classic PVST+ port states and their behavior?
cards.a: Blocking (no forwarding, no MAC learning), Listening (no forwarding, no MAC learning, STP calculation), Learning (no forwarding, learns MACs), and Forwarding (forwards and learns MACs).

cards.q: What are the default classic PVST+ timers?
cards.a: Hello Time = 2 seconds, Forward Delay = 15 seconds, Max Age = 20 seconds. The worst-case timer calculation is 20 + 15 + 15 ≈ 50 seconds, but actual convergence depends on topology.

cards.q: What is the purpose of Max Age and Forward Delay in classic STP?
cards.a: Max Age controls how long received BPDU information is valid before it can be aged out (not simply a blocking timer). Forward Delay controls time spent in Listening and Learning (15 s each).

cards.q: How does classic STP signal a topology change in PVST+?
cards.a: A switch detecting a change sends a TCN BPDU toward the Root; the Root acknowledges and propagates TC information, causing switches to temporarily reduce MAC aging so stale Layer-2 entries are removed faster.

cards.q: What is a key protected-path design pattern using PVST+ load balancing?
cards.a: Different VLANs get different Root Bridges (e.g., Switch A root for VLANs 10,20 and Switch B root for VLANs 30,40) so each dual uplink forwards one set of VLANs and blocks another, using both physical links.

cards.q: Match each STP protection feature to its purpose: PortFast, BPDU Guard, Root Guard, Loop Guard, BPDU Filter.
cards.a: PortFast allows edge ports to transition rapidly; BPDU Guard err-disables a PortFast/edge port if a BPDU is received; Root Guard prevents a port from accepting a superior BPDU and changing root placement; Loop Guard puts a port in loop-inconsistent state when expected BPDUs stop; BPDU Filter suppresses BPDUs and is potentially dangerous if misused.

cards.q: What is the difference between Root Guard and Loop Guard?
cards.a: Root Guard protects root placement by reacting to an unexpected superior BPDU (root-inconsistent). Loop Guard protects against a loop by reacting when expected BPDUs disappear and a non-forwarding port might incorrectly transition to forwarding (loop-inconsistent).

cards.q: How do PVST+, Rapid PVST+, and MST compare in STP logic and number of instances?
cards.a: PVST+ uses 802.1D with one instance per VLAN and slow convergence; Rapid PVST+ uses RSTP with one instance per VLAN and fast convergence; MST uses RSTP with multiple VLANs mapped to fewer instances.

cards.q: Why does MST scale better than PVST+/Rapid PVST+ when there are many VLANs?
cards.a: With e.g. 500 VLANs, PVST+/Rapid PVST+ maintain up to 500 STP instances, while MST maps VLAN groups into a much smaller number of instances, reducing STP control-plane overhead. PVST+/Rapid PVST+ is VLAN-centric; MST is instance-centric.

cards.q: What is the CIST and what does an MST region present to an external PVST+/Rapid PVST+ domain?
cards.a: At an MST boundary the region presents its Common and Internal Spanning Tree (CIST) toward the external STP domain. MST region parameters include Region Name, Revision Number, and VLAN-to-Instance Mapping.

cards.q: What command enables classic PVST+ and what command enables Rapid PVST+?
cards.a: spanning-tree mode pvst enables classic PVST+; spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst enables Rapid PVST+.

cards.q: Which verification commands show STP instances, a specific VLAN, and inconsistent ports?
cards.a: show spanning-tree active shows active STP instances; show spanning-tree vlan 10 shows a VLAN; show spanning-tree inconsistentports shows root-/loop-inconsistent ports; show interfaces trunk verifies native/allowed VLANs.

cards.q: A change to the MST region name, revision, or VLAN mapping will do what to the switches?
cards.a: It can cause the switches to become separate MST regions.

cards.q: Why is Alternate an RSTP role and not a classic PVST+ role?
cards.a: Classic PVST+ uses 802.1D terminology (Root/Designated/Blocking) and does not use Alternate as a formal role; Alternate is an RSTP/Rapid PVST+ port role.

cards.q: Why does classic PVST+ converge more slowly than Rapid PVST+?
cards.a: Classic PVST+ relies on 802.1D timers (Hello 2 s, Max Age 20 s, Forward Delay 15 s), whereas Rapid PVST+ uses RSTP mechanisms such as Proposal/Agreement and alternate roles to converge much faster.
